_note: Summaries of research/SYNTHESIS.md for the site. The full text lives in SYNTHESIS.md. Irish names are provisional.

failure_modes.short: Officials who control social property without owning it become a privileged, self-perpetuating stratum.

cases.text: Trotsky: the bureaucracy as 'policeman' over scarcity (1936)
Voslensky: the nomenklatura's lists and privileges in kind
Michels: the German SPD's 'iron law of oligarchy' (1911)

roots: Control rights concentrated while ownership is nominally collective
Expertise, information and members' limited time favour full-timers
failure_modes.residual: Rotation and lot cost expertise; capped pay may drive skilled people abroad; privilege moves into informal networks.

failure_modes.name_en: Monopoly of power and suppression of pluralism
failure_modes.short: Each 'temporary' restriction removes a channel through which the rulers could be corrected, until only the leadership can check the leadership.

cases.text: Mensheviks and SRs expelled from the soviets, June 1918

roots: Real emergencies make suppression seem reasonable
The party claims to embody the class
Each restriction removes the means to resist the next
failure_modes.residual: Real pluralism includes parties that want to restore capitalism. This design's default answer (a leading party) is its riskiest choice against this failure mode.

failure_modes.short: A single executive office plus the absence of rival authorities produces a cult, which is a product of the system rather than its cause.

cases.text: Khrushchev's 1956 report on the cult of personality

roots: Propaganda resources aimed at one person
Term limits changeable by those they bind
failure_modes.residual: Collective leadership can be slow in a crisis; charisma outside office can't be legislated away.

failure_modes.short: A security service created for an emergency acquires powers to punish and answers only to the leadership. It becomes a state within the state.

cases.text: The Cheka: from investigation to extrajudicial punishment, 1917–18

failure_modes.residual: Real hostile intelligence activity exists; a service too weak to counter it is also a danger.

failure_modes.short: No central planner can gather the local, tacit and fast-changing knowledge an economy runs on (Hayek), or price producer goods (Mises).

cases.text: The calculation debate: Mises, Hayek, Lange

roots: Falsified feedback when targets drive rewards
One centre is a single point of failure
failure_modes.residual: Markets bring back inequality. The argument about democratic, layered coordination is open, not won.

failure_modes.short: Loss-making units are always rescued, so their demand for inputs is 'almost insatiable' and shortage becomes chronic (Kornai).

cases.text: Mondragon refuses a further rescue of Fagor (2013)

roots: Local democratic pressure to protect jobs
failure_modes.residual: Hard budgets mean real closures; one-employer towns will resist.

failure_modes.short: When wages buy little and workers have no voice, effort is withdrawn. The two failed responses are coercion (Stakhanovism) and tacit tolerance.

cases.text: Brezhnev-era slowdown; 'they pretend to pay us…' (origin unverified)

failure_modes.residual: Some people will work less without fear of destitution; the design accepts that as a legitimate choice.

failure_modes.short: Participatory bodies without money or binding power fade into ritual, and full-timers take over.
failure_modes.residual: Entrenching participatory budgets limits future majorities; some people don't want to take part, and must not be punished for it.

failure_modes.short: Enterprise democracy serves the people inside and shuts out those outside: unemployment, regional divergence, two-tier workforces.

cases.text: Yugoslavia: about 15% unemployment by 1985; Slovenia 2.5% vs Kosovo 21% (1965)
Mondragon: about 40% member-owners; Fagor subsidiaries unprotected

failure_modes.residual: Social title plus enterprise use-rights repeats the Djilas problem one level down.

failure_modes.name_en: Counter-revolution from outside or the right
failure_modes.short: Domestic capital and foreign powers use funding, media, strikes by owners and, ultimately, the military.

cases.text: Chile 1970–73: 'make the economy scream'; the truck-owners' strike; the coup
Irish soviets suppressed by both sides, 1920–23

roots: Popular organisation and government strategy split
failure_modes.residual: Every defence against counter-revolution can become FM-02 or FM-04. 'Counter-revolution' must never be a legal charge against peaceful activity.

failure_modes.short: A small open economy depends on outside capital and markets. Ireland's corporation tax depends on a handful of US firms.

cases.text: Ireland: foreign MNCs paid 87% of corporation tax, top 10 paid 56% (2025)

roots: Dependence on outside capital and inputs
failure_modes.residual: The transition will probably make Ireland poorer in GDP terms for a time. The design says so.

failure_modes.short: Those who control but do not own turn control into ownership when they get the chance.
failure_modes.residual: Entrenching social ownership also entrenches it against legitimate democratic change.

failure_modes.short: Strategic disagreement becomes identity; with no legitimate way to disagree, it ends in a split or a purge.

cases.text: Irish left splits: 1970 Official/Provisional; 1992 WP/Democratic Left

failure_modes.residual: Too much tolerance of factions can paralyse decisions.

failure_modes.short: When class politics fails to deliver, national identity becomes the organising grievance, and elites ride it.

cases.text: Connolly's 1897 warning; the Democratic Programme dismissed as 'poetry'

failure_modes.residual: The project is grounded in Irish republican history. That is a strength and a danger at once.

failure_modes.short: Emergencies are real, but the people who hold emergency powers decide when the emergency ends.

cases.text: The Cheka; the 1921 'temporary' ban on factions

roots: A penalty for revoking (Weimar's dissolution trap)
failure_modes.residual: Sunset rules can be gamed by rolling declarations; the design counts new declarations on the same facts as extensions.

failure_modes.short: Output as the measure of legitimacy, and no institution with power to represent ecological limits.

cases.text: Aral Sea; Ecocide in the USSR
Ireland: herd 6.9m, agriculture 38% of emissions; data centres 23% of electricity

failure_modes.residual: Caps on the herd and data centres hit rural incomes and revenue: the constituencies whose loss drives FM-14 and FM-11.

failure_modes.short: The system functions, but daily life feels drab and ritualised, access depends on connections, and people stop believing.

cases.text: Kern & Hainmueller: entertainment stabilised the GDR

failure_modes.residual: Variety pulls against ecological sufficiency. A democratic system can lose legitimacy and be voted out, and that must be accepted.

failure_modes.short: Women are brought into paid work while unpaid care stays theirs and stays invisible.

cases.text: Lenin and Kollontai's promise; the 1936 abortion ban
GDR: 78–91% female employment; housework still women's
Ireland: Art. 41.2; 2024 care referendum 73.9% No; 299,128 carers

failure_modes.residual: Socialised care can slide into institutionalisation, a fear sharpened by Ireland's history.
